doc.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014

title: Listening: Ellington, Mingus and Max Roach on Money Jungle
summary: Harper responds to a Money Jungle clip, recalls Max Roach as his start in music, and discusses Roach's sound.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Okay, let me try another one here.
An interesting combination of people: Ellington and Mingus and Max Roach. I wouldn’t have guessed that that would gel.
Yeah, I would, I would. What was that, “Money Jungle?”

Yeah it would because I think — I never met Duke Ellington or Mingus. I knew Max, I knew Max well. Max was really my start into the music. And he was a big help in my career. But just knowing, like I said, there again, understanding him, what he played for, his intentions and everything, his love for the music, his love for history. I knew how, and when you hear all of those guys talking about Duke Ellington, there’s a deep respect. You know what I mean? So with guys like that I don’t care who everybody else is you’re going to come and you’re going to find a way. Look, we’re playing with Duke Ellington. I mean it’s like you figure if Louis Armstrong came along and, whoever he wanted to hire, the guy’s going to find a way to empty my glass and we’re going to get filled up and

we’re going to make this work you know. So those guys, their intent and their love for the music, you figure that’s going to carry. Mingus or another great bassist and a great composer, and you have an opportunity to work with Duke Ellington, of course.
Wasn’t there a story about Ellington had to let Charles Mingus go or something? He got into a — oh there’s some anecdote about he got into a hassle with Juan Tizol.
Yeah it’s out there. It sounded like Max was playing with really thin sticks to me, that sound. Is that an assumption that I can make or don’t you really know?

I never really thought about it. It could be. But I know too, I can tell the drums are tuned kind of high. The way Max plays, I mean, he’s another one, the sound always came through. But he’s another one, he was a good composer, and when he played the drums he was always composing.
